summary: Roma and Lazio have both made unbeaten starts to the Serie A season, giving those in the Italian capital dreams of a ScudettoAfter nine games in 28 days, Gian Piero Gasperini finally got a moment to pause and reflect on Sunday night.
Gasperini’s Roma thumped Sassuolo 3-0 on Saturday, bouncing back from a midweek loss to Manchester United.
More importantly, Roma’s victory meant they remained undefeated in domestic competition this season.

stories.title: Felix Nmecha’s faith is forcing Borussia Dortmund into an uncomfortable debate
summary: Midfielder’s spectacular strikes rescued a frustrating day, only for celebrations to reignite dialogue that has followed him through his careerIt was just what they needed at just the right time.
BVB have enjoyed a largely excellent start to the season, are unbeaten and level on points with Bayern Munich at the top; Bayern lead, unsurprisingly, thanks to their superior goal difference.

It is a gap which has been widened by Dortmund being far from prolific, a facet which looked as if it might undercut their efforts to roll over their visitors on Saturday, especially in the absence of the injured centre-forward Serhou Guirassy.

summary: Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be.

They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30.
They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week.

stories.title: Ramla Ali wins first world titles at 36 with highly controversial split decision
summary: British-Somali boxer claims first world titles in TexasKreps outlands Ali but loses disputed split decisionBaumgardner wins 135lb belt as Dubois feud heats upAustralia’s Nicolson retains junior featherweight titleBritish-Somali boxer Ramla Ali became a world champion for the first time at the age of 36 on Sunday night after escaping with a highly contentious 10-round split decision over former sparring partner Mikiah Kreps to claim the vacant WBO and IBF women’s junior featherweight titles in Arlington, Texas.Ali, who grew up in east London after fleeing Somalia’s civil war with her family and went on to become the first boxer to represent the African country at the Olympics, completed her remarkable journey to the top of the 122lb division at College Park Center on her second attempt at a world championship – but only after a controversial verdict rewarding her for a fight that appeared to be largely controlled by her opponent.

stories.title: ‘I’m going to tell the truth. Screw this!’ Billie Jean King at 82 on coming out, tearing up tennis – and her one big regret
summary: On the day we speak, the list includes her nephew and her wife, Ilana Kloss, who like her is a decorated former tennis player.

And, as ever, Susan Williams, who was in King’s fifth grade class at school in Long Beach, California, when she was 11 years old.“Do you want to play tennis?” Williams asked one day. “What’s tennis?” King responded.

Although basketball was a big part of her early childhood, Williams was the first person to tell her about tennis. “She said: ‘You get to run, jump and hit a ball.’ And I went: ‘Oh, three of my favourite things.’” Continue reading...
